_note: 格式样例。清单条目是主角自己的口气；对话框四种行：narration / inner / sfx / speaker。克总不走对话框。

say.t: Raining. Working from home is not a bad choice.
A glass of water on the desk, cold. Two screens, black.
A new day's work starts at the power button.
Ding-dong.
Two things at the door: a bag of braised chicken rice, and a cardboard box with no sender.
The box has a recipient. It is your name.
You put it between the two screens, into the gap. It wedges there. It does not fall.
Older than this room by a whole era.
The light goes out, or rather, you turn the screen off. The room sinks all at once.
There is a point of light in that dark. Not the chick's screen; the chick is lower down.
It sits in the middle of the gap, small, pinkish. You count to seven. It is still there.
Pink. Nothing in this room of mine is pink.
You close your eyes. First a grey-white behind the lids, then, bit by bit, a room. Not this one.
In the dream you remember: this one is yours. A knock-off of a knock-off, bought at a street stall, one chick and nothing else. You treasured it.
The tail end of summer; the fan chops the light into bright and dark. First week of school, second lesson, test papers handed back.
Come and get yours when I call your name.
Ninety-six. Since first grade you had never scored under a hundred. In that very second it chirped in your desk drawer.
(whispering) Your chick's hungry.
The whole class heard it. Nobody turned round. Neither did you.
What is in that drawer. Bring it here.
You bring it up. She doesn't look at it. She looks at your paper.
Ninety-six. Toys rot the mind.
Evening, the dinner table. The paper lies open next to the dishes.
Your teacher phoned.
Not about you. About that thing. It stays with her till the end of term.
It needs feeding three times a day.
It's a game. Nobody starves. Eat.
On the last day of term she handed it back with your report card. The report first: a hundred. Then it, its screen already the grave.
See. She was right to take it.
It was taken. I did not stop feeding it.
Later you pressed the little hole on the back. Nothing. It stayed a grave.
For a long time, whenever the battery was nearly gone, you put in a new one. Thinking that one day the chick would come back.
Today is over.

items.text: Press the tower under the desk. Boot up.
Into the screen. Glance at the messages.

say.t: The boss's message is on top again.
A 41-second voice note. Opening it will cost more than 41 seconds.

items.text: Pick up the phone, order lunch.

say.t: Phone back on the desk.

items.text: Go get it at the door.

say.t: Ding-dong.
Delivery. And something else.

items.text: The table by the window. Eat.

say.t: No coriander. Lao Zhou ordered it.

items.text: That box by the bed. Open it.
Change one number in the receivables.
Thing A: Future Intelligence, the technical story.

say.t: What you can say back is a few lines, like a very small table.

items.text: Go to the desk and take a look.
Top right of the screen. Shut down.
That one in the bottom right. Talk to it a while.
